b.d: Maker of throwers and high-output lights such as the L19 and X series.
Chicago firm, founded as the Mantle Lamp Company, maker of Aladdin mantle lamps from 1912.
British maker of the spring-balanced Anglepoise lamp, licensed by George Carwardine to Herbert Terry & Sons in 1934; owned by the Terry family.
Lighting company founded by Gino Sarfatti; maker of the original Sputnik-type model 2003.
Milan design-lighting maker founded in 1960 by Ernesto Gismondi and Sergio Mazza; privately held.
Company founded by Alessandro Sarfatti that re-edits Gino Sarfatti designs.
Lighting maker in Åhus, Sweden, led by Anders Pehrson 1963–78.
French crystal house in Baccarat, Lorraine, making chandeliers since 1824.
Murano glassworks of the Barovier family (recorded from 1324), named Barovier&Toso since 1942.
Taiwanese electronics maker that introduced the monitor light bar.
Brooklyn maker of camp stoves, lanterns, headlamps and solar power.
American maker of climbing, skiing and outdoor gear including headlamps.
American camping brand whose pressure lantern became the standard camp and farm light.
Budget brand whose S2+ is the standard modding host.
French publisher holding the rights to the Lampe Gras, reissued since 2008.
Austrian lighting maker.
Brand of H. G. McFaddin & Co. under which the green-shaded banker's lamp was sold.
Hank Wang's brand sold through Intl-Outdoor (with Noctigon); D4V2 uses the community Anduril firmware.
Chinese flashlight maker with PD, TK, LR and E series.
German hurricane-lantern maker whose trademark the Petromax group acquired in 2014.
Italian design-lighting maker, producer of the Castiglioni classics; owned by Design Holding, jointly controlled by Investindustrial and The Carlyle Group (formed November 2018).
Italian design-lighting maker, originally from Murano; an independent lighting house led by founder and president Carlo Urbinati.
Danish furniture maker that owns the Kaiser Idell brand; wholly owned by Chr. Augustinus Fabrikker through Skandinavisk Holding since 1 July 2025.
Current producer of the US Army and Marines' MX-991/U angle-head flashlight.
Original producer of the Castiglioni Luminator floor lamp of 1955.
Shenzhen maker of low-cost app-controlled LED strips, bulbs and light panels.
Danish design company producing the Bestlite range.
New York firm of George W. Hansen; swing-arm lamps made by Metalarte, Barcelona; later acquired by Hinson Lighting.
American furniture maker and current producer of the Nelson Bubble lamps.
Original maker of George Nelson's Bubble lamps.
Swedish flat-pack furniture and home-goods retailer with a large lamp range.
Munich studio of lighting designer Ingo Maurer, founded as Design M; Foscarini bought 90% of the shares in May 2022 and Sarah Utermöhlen kept 10%.
Family-owned Viennese glass and chandelier maker; co-developed the first electric chandeliers with Edison.
Lyon maker of jointed steel lamps, named after founder Jean-Louis Domecq's initials.
Italian maker of furniture and lamps in moulded plastics.
Californian maker founded by Donald Keller and Frank Patti; its aluminium baton-torch set the duty-light pattern; merged into Streamlight 1983.
Solingen maker founded by Harald and Rainer Opolka as Zweibrüder; known for the focusable P series.
Danish lighting maker known for Poul Henningsen and Verner Panton designs; owned by Design Holding, jointly controlled by Investindustrial and The Carlyle Group (formed November 2018).
Oslo lamp maker founded by Jac Jacobsen, known for the L-1 architect lamp; part of Glamox.
Torch brand of Mag Instrument, Inc. (Ontario, California), founded by Anthony Maglica; the Maglite appeared in 1979.
Small American business run by Gene and Cathy Malkoff; makes MDC lights and M61 light engines used in other makers' torches.
Italian lighting maker, producer of Gae Aulenti's Pipistrello.
Dutch design label founded by Marcel Wanders and Casper Vissers.
Maker of small luxury lights in aluminium, titanium and copper.
Toronto LED lighting company founded by three University of Toronto engineers, known for modular light panels.
Chinese maker of the EDC, TIKI/TINI keychain and Tiny Monster lines.
Small-batch custom maker of machined 18350 lights.
Chinese maker known for magnetic-charging lights.
Milan lighting maker, producer of Magistretti's Atollo.
Gifu lantern maker, original manufacturer of Isamu Noguchi's Akari lamps.
German lighting maker.
Brand of Max Graetz's kerosene pressure lantern, revived as Petromax GmbH in 2010.
French maker of climbing and caving equipment and headlamps, based in Crolles near Grenoble; founded by caver Fernand Petzl.
Dutch electronics brand; its consumer lamps include the Hue smart range.
Czech crystal company whose Preciosa Lighting continues chandelier making in Kamenický Šenov.
Brooklyn lamp firm, the leading American hurricane-lantern maker, now based in Hong Kong.
Murano furnace founded as Seguso Vetri d'Arte; sold in 1974 and bought back by the family in 2007.
Budget maker of throwers, EDC and right-angle lights.
Milan lighting maker of the post-war era, revived in the 21st century.
Eagleville, Pennsylvania maker of duty, tactical and weapon lights; absorbed Kel-Lite in 1983.
Fountain Valley, California maker founded as Laser Products Corporation; renamed SureFire, LLC in 2000.
American maker of the Tensor high-intensity lamp.
Louis Comfort Tiffany's New York studio, making leaded-glass lamps from 1893 until it closed in the late 1920s.
British maker of paraffin pressure lamps, lanterns and heaters.
London design brand of designer Tom Dixon.
Redmond, Washington, maker of candle lanterns and candles.
Murano glassworks founded by Paolo Venini and Giacomo Cappellin; owned by Damiani since 2016.
Swiss company producing Jean Prouvé designs including the Potence lamp.
Halifax maker of Vapalux pressure lanterns; brand sold to a Korean maker in 2010.
Chinese electronics maker; its monitor light bar is a tested budget rival to the ScreenBar.
Maker of compact side-switch SC lights and H headlamps with neutral and high-CRI emitters.
Re-edits Serge Mouille's 1950s lamps in France.
Dutch lighting company spun off from Philips in 2016, named Philips Lighting N.V. until 2018; owns Philips Hue, WiZ and Color Kinetics.
Osram was formed in 1919 from the lighting businesses of Auergesellschaft, Siemens & Halske and AEG; ams took it over in July 2020.
Lighting business sold by General Electric to Savant Systems on 1 July 2020.
Home automation company based in Hyannis, Massachusetts, which bought GE Lighting in 2020.
Released the first commercial white LED lamp for homes in 2007.
Wi-Fi smart bulb brand; Feit Electric bought the LIFX assets from Lifi Labs, Inc. in August 2022.
Lighting firm with about 40 years of history that bought the LIFX brand in 2022.
Italian design-lighting maker of Hope, designed by Francisco Gomez Paz and Paolo Rizzatto.
Italian design-lighting maker of the Anima lamp, a 2024 Compasso d'Oro winner.
Italian lighting company that produces the Biga lamp, a 2024 Compasso d'Oro winner.
Italian producer of the E63 table lamp by Umberto Riva, with FontanaArte, per Lightology.
Italian lighting maker of the Bilia and E63 lamps, per Lightology.
